title: PR observability + lint-bot scratchpad
text:
Purpose:
 - Capture ideas for an automated PR observability assistant (lint + lightweight checks + flake detection) for faster reviews and post-merge signals.
 - This is a scratchpad for tradeoffs, heuristics, and UI/UX for reviewer-facing flags.

Motivation / problem statements:
 - Reviewers spend time guessing whether a CI failure was transient vs a real regression.
 - Large PRs slip past checks because flaky tests masked real regressions (low signal-to-noise).
 - We lack quick visibility in the PR summary for: historical flake rate, infra region impacted, and rollout risk score.

Core ideas (high level):
 1) PR-level observability panel (inline with PR overview) that surfaces:
    - Last 5 CI runs: pass/fail and flaky markers.
    - Test-suite heatmap: which packages/modules changed vs failing tests.
    - Estimated rollout risk: heuristic combining churn size, touched APIs, test-failure history (0-100).
 2) Lint-bot rules for PR metadata:
    - Require 'impact' label or short summary for API changes.
    - Warn on >3 newly added integration tests in a single PR; suggest splitting.
    - Flag changes that touch runtime/serving code without a perf benchmark.
 3) Flake detector: lightweight service that aggregates recent failures and marks a failure as 'likely flake' if:
    - same test failed in >=2 distinct recent runs but only for one commit and other similar tests passed, OR
    - infra-exit codes indicate transient infra (docker pull, timeout, VM preemption), OR
    - failure stack traces match known flaky patterns (network/timeouts/assert timing).

Quick review checklist (for humans) to show in PR sidebar:
 - [ ] Small description of behaviour change + quick reasoning for perf impact
 - [ ] Link to related evals / prompt-suite (if generator/LLM change)
 - [ ] CI baseline run attached (if perf-affecting)
 - [ ] Author verified locally: unit tests and one integration smoke run
 - [ ] If tests added: justify coverage vs flaky risk (unit vs integration)

Heuristics / scoring sketch (for the risk score):
 - base = min(50, 5 * changed_files_count)
 - +20 if touching serving/runtime or authentication layers
 - +20 if tests added > 5 and >20 new lines of test code
 - -15 if change is doc-only or comments
 - +10 if recent failures in same module in last 7 days
 - cap at 95; floor at 5
Notes: score should be transparent and shown with contributing factors.

Bot actions (what the automated assistant can do):
 - Post a summary comment with the observability panel snapshots and risk score when PR opened and on each push.
 - Auto-assign 'flake' label when flake detector confidence > 0.8; notify author with suggested next steps.
 - Suggest splitting PRs that exceed churn thresholds (files, LOC, package boundaries).
 - Offer 're-run flaky jobs' button for maintainers (rate-limited).

UI/UX mock notes (quick):
 - Compact badge: [Risk: 42] [Flake: yes] [Heatmap: 3 hotspots] placed under PR title. Clicking expands full panel.
 - Each entry in heatmap links to failing test logs and last green commit.

Automation infra thoughts:
 - Flake detector can be serverless function that consumes CI events + a short lookback (7d). Keep state minimal (test -> last N outcomes).
 - Store historic flake metrics in a lightweight timeseries store (Influx/Clickhouse) for aggregated views. Alternatively, use GitHub checks + annotations for per-PR transient info.
 - Danger: any automated label must be reversible and include audit logs (audit trail in PR thread).

Edge cases / unresolved questions:
 - How to treat long-running integration tests (10+ min) in the flake model? run-level labels or test-level?
 - When to prefer human triage over bot suppression for flaky but high-risk failures?
 - Privacy: logs sometimes contain customer request ids; we should mask before surfacing.
 - Rate limiting: avoid noisy bot comments on huge refactor churn (thresholds).

Short-term roadmap (MVP):
 - Phase 0 (1 week): simple PR comment bot that posts last 3 CI results and a link to the raw logs (no scoring).
 - Phase 1 (4 wks): add flake detector with simple heuristics (same-test repeat within 7d), risk-score prototype, and heatmap for changed packages. Hook to GitHub checks.
 - Phase 2 (8 wks): UI/console in DevX dashboard, historical flake trends, re-run button, and finer-grained rules.

Implementation notes / sample GH Action idea (pseudo):
 name: pr-observability
 on: [pull_request, workflow_run]
 jobs:
   collect:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/github-script@v6
         with:
           script: |
             // fetch last 3 workflow_runs for this PR, summarize statuses, post comment
             // call flake-detector service for analysis

Todo list (next actions for me / us):
 - [ ] prototype comment format and post in #devx-pr-bots for feedback (Maya)
 - [ ] build tiny flake detector lambda and run against last 30 days of CI to get baseline (Liam)
 - [ ] draft PR UI mock and get PM buy-in for risk-score transparency

Notes-to-self (short scribbles):
 - Keep the initial rules conservative: false positives are costly (annoying reviewers).
 - Consider an opt-out label for repos that want no bot noise (e.g., legacy infra).
 - Track bot adoption: PRs with bot annotation should have reduced time-to-merge if helpful.

References / links for heuristics inspiration:
 - flake-db paper notes: https://example.com/flake-db (placeholder)
 - prior internal thread: slack:#ci-cops 2025-06-02

-- end of scratchpad --
